subject: Calculating effort for annual density estimates

messages.author: 1f59ab9a90651ec7
messages.subject: Calculating effort for annual density estimates
parts:
Hello,

I had a question based on the way this analysis is conducted.
https://groups.google.com/g/distance-sampling/c/t77OHskxyso/m/hWBP_DftAQAJ

I have surveys from 2020-2023 and wanted to get density estimates by year. I don't have enough detections across all years to build separate detection functions, so I thought to follow the method outlined here to have years as strata, but I ran into a few questions about how best to allocate effort. Some of the transects were not surveyed all year due to weather constraints, so effort across the years is a bit uneven. When I ran the analysis to get overall densities, I multiplied the effort by the number of times the transect was conducted; I then used this same data frame and used year as strata. My question is, when I do it this way, am I overestimating effort through the years? The estimated numbers do add up to what I get when I run it with the region, though. When I corrected for effort yearly, the estimates seemed slightly off from the main model.  
I have attached a reference of my data frame and the results from the models I ran with effort accounted for in different ways. I have a feeling I have this wrong somewhere!

Thanks so much for the help!

messages.subject: Re: Calculating effort for annual density estimates
parts:
Hi all,
Copied below are Eric's comments and suggestions for this analysis and my question

If you are treating year as strata, it is fine if effort differs between years. Imagine your strata were geographic; separating the study area into three geographic pieces. There is no reason that each geographic stratum would have the same amount of effort. Therefore, I don't think your analysis with effort kept the same is reasonable.
Thanks for the spreadsheet. I get the same result as the third page of your Word document from the following code (except your Word document labels the result as a hazard rate when you really fitted a half normal without adjustments):

library(readxl)
isha <- read_xlsx("E:/troubleshoot/Isha/Datasheet.xlsx", sheet = 1)
names(isha)[2] <- "Study.Area"
names(isha)[3] <- "Strata"
names(isha)[5] <- "Area"
names(isha)[7] <- "Region.Label"
names(isha)[10] <- "distance"
names(isha)[15] <- "Effort"

library(Distance)
cu <- convert_units("meter", "kilometer", "square kilometer")
hn5 <- ds(isha, key="hn", adjustment = NULL, 
          truncation = "5%", convert_units = cu)
summary(hn5)

I made Effort in the analysis the Yearly.effort column. Hope that makes the analysis clear

Also another point to note, we used a pooled detection function across all years. But Eric's suggestion is to try and compute a separate detection function for all the three years and then compare the models.

I should also mention that the analysis carried out assumes detection probability is constant across years. If detectability does differ between years, the results from that model will be biased.
You should also fit a model with year as a covariate and contrast that AIC with the constant probability model:

library(readxl)

isha <- read_xlsx("E:/troubleshoot/Isha/Datasheet.xlsx", sheet = 1)
names(isha)[2] <- "Study.Area"
names(isha)[3] <- "Strata"
names(isha)[5] <- "Area"
names(isha)[7] <- "Region.Label"
names(isha)[10] <- "distance"
names(isha)[15] <- "Effort"

library(Distance)
cu <- convert_units("meter", "kilometer", "square kilometer")
hn5 <- ds(isha, key="hn", adjustment = NULL, 
          truncation = "5%", convert_units = cu)
summary(hn5)

isha$Region.Label <- as.factor(isha$Region.Label)
hn.year.covar <- ds(isha, key="hn", 
                    truncation = "5%", convert_units = cu,
                    formula=~Region.Label)

summarize_ds_models(hn5, hn.year.covar)
# You will see that the model with year as a covariate 
#          has a considerably smaller AIC

plot(hn.year.covar)
add.df.covar.line(hn.year.covar, data=data.frame(Region.Label=as.factor(2020)),
                  lwd=2, lty=1, col="darkred")
add.df.covar.line(hn.year.covar, data=data.frame(Region.Label=as.factor(2022)),
                  lwd=2, lty=1, col="darkblue")
add.df.covar.line(hn.year.covar, data=data.frame(Region.Label=as.factor(2023)),
                  lwd=2, lty=1, col="darkgreen")
legend("topright", legend=c(2020, 2022, 2023), 
       col=c("darkred", "darkblue", "darkgreen"), lwd=2, lty=1)

# the model fit is not very good and the 2022 detection function 
# is much different
